# @amykit/plugin-terminal

Drives an interactive terminal program through terminal-use: run it, type, press keys, wait for text and read the screen.

A plugin for [amy](https://github.com/nicolasmelo1/amy).

Use it when a proof has to drive an interactive terminal program, such as an editor or a CLI that prompts. It adds terminal operations a prove scenario can call: run a program, type, press keys, wait for text and read the screen. It needs the terminal-use CLI on the machine.

## What it extends

|  |  |
| :-- | :-- |
| Ports | _none_ |
| Actions | _none_ |
| Operations | `terminal.kill`, `terminal.press`, `terminal.run`, `terminal.screen`, `terminal.type`, `terminal.wait` |
| Commands | _none_ |
| Events | _none_ |
| Environment | _none_ |

## Install

```sh
amy add @amykit/plugin-terminal
```

Then name it in `~/.amy/config.yaml`:

```yaml
workflows:
  your-profile:
    plugins:
      - "@amykit/plugin-terminal"
```

## Configuration

```yaml
plugins:
  "@amykit/plugin-terminal":
    binary: "tu"
    session: "amy"
    timeoutMs: 60000
```

| Setting | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `binary` | `string` | no | `tu` | the terminal-use command, or a path to it |
| `session` | `string` | no | `amy` | the terminal-use session every operation drives, so steps of one scenario share one program |
| `timeoutMs` | `number` | no | `60000` | how long one terminal-use command may run, past any wait it was asked for |

Every field is checked at boot against the schema this package declares. A key that is
not one of the above is a refusal naming the plugin and the key, not a setting that
silently never applied.
